results.title: The worst COP ever? Climate talks collapse in chaos
results.content: The COP31 climate talks ended in failure Sunday as a contentious deal collapsed over fossil fuels and the summit in Turkey stretched into record overtime. The final agreement was rejected in a chaotic finale to a UN climate summit that ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world. France 24’s Douglas Herbert takes a look at whether the failure to reach an agreement makes COP31 the most disappointing climate summit to date.

results.title: Ukraine-Russia peace talks: Row over who will represent the EU
results.content: As Russia and Ukraine continue to trade strikes a row is erupting over who Europe should send to any future peace talks with the two countries along with the US. The EU's High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas is being squeezed out in favour of foreign ministers of five of Europe's major countries, a sign, says France 24’s correspondent Dave Keating, that the EU still lacks a common foreign policy.

results.title: Odesa pupils switch to remote learning as Russia pounds Ukraine’s energy grid
results.content: Schools in Odesa will switch to remote teaching after Russian strikes gravely damaged the energy grid in the major Ukrainian Black Sea port city. Russia has carried out a wide-ranging campaign of strikes against Ukraine's energy infrastructure, with the prospect of another freezing wartime winter looming.

results.title: Zelensky says Ukraine sank Russian warship off Libya
results.content: President Volodymyr Zelensky has confirmed that Ukraine was behind the sinking of a ⁠Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port on Sunday in an attack involving seven naval drones. Zelensky said Ukraine also struck a Russian cargo ship the MV Angara, which he said Russia had ⁠used to transport weapons.

results.title: 'Let down on all sides': Pacific island nations express despair over COP31 failure
results.content: Several Pacific island nations expressed despair and disappointment Monday over the failure of the UN climate talks to reach a final agreement on tackling the climate crisis. Small nations in the Pacific are among the world's most vulnerable to the rising sea levels brought on my man-made global warming.

results.title: Ligue 1: Marseille lose to Le Mans after being two goals up at home
results.content: Olympique de Marseille suffered a home defeat against Le Mans (3–2). Having led 2-0 after 40 minutes thanks to goals from Gouiri (33’) and Paixão (40’), OM collapsed.

results.title: Live: Zelensky confirms Ukraine’s military struck Russian ships in Libyan waters
results.content: Ukraine’s military was responsible for drone attacks on two Russian vessels at the Libyan port of Benghazi Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed Monday. The president alleged that the Russian corvette Merkury had been sunk in the attack. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

results.title: Thousands rally in Istanbul against Turkey’s crackdown on opposition and media
results.content: Thousands marched in Istanbul on Sunday against a widening crackdown on Turkey’s opposition and independent media, days after police raided Sozcu TV and arrested senior staff. The main opposition Yeni Parti organised the protest after authorities installed a government-appointed trustee at the broadcaster, following similar moves against other independent outlets.

results.title: Christmas market returns to Paris' Champs Elysées
results.content: France 24's Jamie Smith-Maillet reports from the opening of the Paris Christmas market on the Champs Elysées.

results.title: France's far-right leader Le Pen denies receiving secrets from civil servant
results.content: French far-right leader Marine Le Pen Sunday denied receiving confidential information from a civil servant suspected of leaking details of investigations to her National Rally (RN) party, while acknowledging she could not say whether others in the party had benefited.

results.title: COP31 climate talks in Turkey collapse
results.content: EU member states on Sunday objected to adopting an 11th-hour deal that omitted explicit references to fossil fuels, the bloc's presidency said. The issue remains a major point of contention at the summit, which is taking place amid soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the war in Iran.

results.title: Drone strikes hit homes, United Nations building in Sudan's capital
results.content: Drone strikes damaged residential homes and a United Nations building in Sudan's capital Khartoum early Sunday, with the army accusing neighbouring Ethiopia of launching the attacks. The strikes came as drone warfare intensifies in the country's conflict, now in its fourth year.

results.title: Russian ship attacked near Benghazi in suspected drone attack
results.content: Authorities in divided Libya's east said a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi port was hit on Sunday in a suspected drone attack, causing a blast but no casualties. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the strike, but it comes as Ukrainian forces have stepped up their long-range barrages against Russia far beyond the front lines.

results.title: Israel’s Eisenkot slams ‘Jewish terrorism’ after attacks by settlers in West Bank
results.content: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot on Sunday condemned arson attacks by settlers on Palestinian villages in the West Bank as “Jewish terrorism”. Israeli police said they opened an investigation into the attacks, which came nearly a month after an inconclusive election stripped incumbent Prime Minister ⁠Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority.

results.title: Democrat Hubbard wins North Carolina recount, clinching historic House majority
results.content: Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the US House of Representatives from North Carolina on Sunday after defeating veteran Republican Virginia Foxx, who chairs the powerful House Rules Committee. His victory gave Democrats their best general election result in decades, winning at least 258 seats in the 2026 US midterms.

results.title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
results.content: A Russian navy corvette docked at the Benghazi naval base ​in eastern Libya was hit on Sunday by a Ukrainian sea drone, according to local officials, hours before a cargo ship was also hit by a sea drone in a second attack. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday confirmed that his country's military was behind the strikes.

results.title: Burnham, 'Brejoin' & the Ghosts of Brexit
results.content: “The people of Britain have spoken, and the answer is: we are out.” The words of David Dimbleby at 4.40am on 24 June 2016, as the Brexit referendum result became clear. But nearly a decade on, is Britain changing its mind? Prime Minister Andy Burnham has reopened talks with Brussels, exploring options for a closer relationship with the EU. But the move has drawn criticism from key figures behind Brexit, including Theresa May and Boris Johnson. So what is driving this rethink, and where might it lead? France 24's Gavin Lee speaks to John McTernan, veteran Labour strategist and former adviser to Tony Blair.

results.title: Le Pen denies receiving leaked information from French interior ministry official
results.content: French far-right leader Marine Le Pen on Sunday said she did not receive, nor ask for, confidential information on an investigation into her party from a senior interior ministry official. She however could not say if other party members had benefited from the leaks. Hugues Moutouh, the civil servant under suspicion, has denied the allegations and asked to be relieved of his duties pending a probe.

results.title: Ligue 1: PSG extend winning run at Nice (3-2) but lose Désiré Doué to injury
results.content: A bittersweet victory for PSG at Nice on Saturday evening. The Parisians strengthened their grip on top spot in Ligue 1, but lost Désiré Doué for several months after the forward suffered a serious knee injury.

results.title: Drone strikes hit homes and UN building in Sudan's Khartoum
results.content: Drone strikes damaged residential homes and a United Nations building in Sudan's capital Khartoum early Sunday, with the army accusing neighbouring Ethiopia of launching the attacks. The strikes came as drone warfare intensifies in the country's conflict, now in its fourth year.

results.title: West Bank attacks: Opposition leader Eisenkot decries "Jewish terrorism"
results.content: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were set on fire in three villages in the occupied West Bank. Israeli soldiers were deployed to the area following the attacks, which local residents said were carried out by Israeli settlers. Gadi Eisenkot, a rival of outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, condemned the acts on X, describing them as “Jewish terrorism”. Antonia Kerrigan reports.

results.title: Russian strike kills 2 in Kyiv
results.content: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in the village of Dymer, just north of Kyiv, on Sunday, killing at least two people and wounding four others. The morning strike destroyed a five-storey building, while rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child. At least 11 others are believed to remain trapped under the rubble.

results.title: The week in pictures: Xi hosts Trump and Putin, COP31 and new French protests
results.content: From the unprecedented Shenzhen summit in China that saw President Xi Jinping host his US and Russian counterparts, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, to tough talks at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey and another week of French protests over the cost of living, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the most striking images from the past week.

results.title: 'It can take years': Why the AI Riemann proof is far from settled
results.content: Artificial intelligence claimed another major scalp in maths on Friday, as Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge published what he says is proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a Millennium Prize Problem, in 17 million lines of code that no human has read in full. Physicist Tony Padilla tells Tech 24 that verification could take years, and that Alpöge should share how he got there.
